targets.label: Moon, south pole
targets.has_ice_source: Li, S. et al. (2018). Direct evidence of surface exposed water ice in the lunar polar regions. PNAS 115(36), 8907-8912. doi:10.1073/pnas.1802345115
targets.summary: Lunar south polar region, south of 85° S: permanently shadowed craters with water ice and areas of near-continuous illumination. Destination of the crewed Artemis missions.
unreplicable: Gravity of 1.62 m/s² (one sixth of Earth's)
Solar and cosmic radiation with no atmosphere or magnetic field to stop it
Permanently shadowed craters, much colder than anywhere on Earth
notes: The lunar day lasts about 29.5 Earth days: the temperature range is the cycle's maximum minus its minimum, not an Earth daily range
The ice fraction is 1 by definition (the target has ice); it is not the fraction of the surface covered

slope_deg.source: LOLA LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ (LRO), NASA PGDA, downsampled to 1 km

roughness_m.source: LOLA LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ (LRO), NASA PGDA, downsampled to 1 km

tmin_c.source: Williams, J.-P. et al. (2017). The global surface temperatures of the Moon as measured by the Diviner Lunar Radiometer Experiment. Icarus 283, 300-325. doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2016.08.012. Mean minimum poleward of 85°: 50 K. Standard deviation estimated by the team (unpublished)

trange_c.source: Williams, J.-P. et al. (2017), Icarus 283, 300-325. Mean maximum 202 K and mean minimum 50 K poleward of 85°: 152 K. Standard deviation estimated by the team (unpublished)

precip_mm.source: By definition: no atmosphere, no rain

targets.label: Mars, Jezero crater
targets.has_ice_source: Morgan, G. A. et al. (2021). Availability of subsurface water-ice resources in the northern mid-latitudes of Mars. Nature Astronomy 5, 230-236. Accessible ice lies north of about 35-40° N; Jezero (18.4° N) is outside
targets.summary: Crater about 45 km across with an ancient lake and its delta; landing site of the Perseverance rover (center near 18.38° N, 77.58° E).
unreplicable: Carbon dioxide atmosphere with less than 1% of Earth's pressure
Much higher ultraviolet and cosmic radiation

tmin_c.source: MEDA (Perseverance), ground temperature: minimum of 191 K on sol 189 (Savijärvi, H. et al. 2023, JGR Planets, doi:10.1029/2022JE007438) and about 200 K near aphelion, Ls 66-92 (Atri, D. et al. 2022, MNRAS, arXiv:2204.12850). Mean 193 K; standard deviation estimated by the team

trange_c.source: MEDA (Perseverance): daily amplitude of 86 K on sol 189 (191 to 277 K; Savijärvi et al. 2023) and about 60 K near aphelion (Atri et al. 2022). Standard deviation estimated by the team

dust_aod.source: Mastcam-Z and MEDA (Perseverance): dust optical depth of 0.4 to 0.5 outside storms during the first 250 sols (Rodriguez-Manfredi, J. A. et al. 2023, Nature Geoscience 16, 19-28, doi:10.1038/s41561-022-01084-0); up to 1.4 in the January 2022 storm (Lemmon, M. T. et al. 2022, Geophysical Research Letters, doi:10.1029/2022GL100126). Measured at 880 nm; Martian dust changes only a few points between the visible and 880 nm. Standard deviation estimated by the team

wind_ms.source: MEDA (Perseverance): mean daytime wind of about 4 m/s at 1.5 m height (Newman, C. E. et al. 2022, Science Advances 8, eabn3783, doi:10.1126/sciadv.abn3783). On Earth, MERRA-2 gives the wind at about 10 m. Standard deviation estimated by the team
